holiday-robotics-2026.tagline: A robotics company supplying wheeled humanoid robots to automobile, semiconductor, and logistics factories.

founders.background: Engineer from Seoul National University. Co-founded AI vision inspection startup SuaLab in 2013 and sold it to US-based Cognex for approx. $195M (approx. KRW 230B) in 2019. After leading the deep learning engineering division at Cognex for about 4 years, founded Holiday Robotics in March 2024.
founders.notable_achievement: Sold SuaLab in the largest foreign acquisition of a Korean startup (at the time). Led the world's largest industrial deep learning vision engineering organization at Cognex.

Planning to expand R&D headcount to over 100 with Series A funding. Won the Outstanding Paper Award for FlashSAC paper at RSS (Robotics: Science and Systems) 2026.

product.summary: FRIDAY is an industrial humanoid robot with a wheeled base and a 64-degree-of-freedom (DoF) upper body. 40 of the total DoF are allocated to the two hands (20 DoF each) to focus on precise manipulation, and the front of the palms are equipped with tactile sensors at 250Hz with 0.05N sensitivity. It employs a proprietary Vision-Language-Skill (VLS) architecture that selects pre-validated motor control primitives, prioritizing safety in industrial environments.
product.problem_statement: Repetitive assembly, sorting, and transport tasks in automotive, semiconductor, and logistics factories still rely on human hands. Existing industrial robot arms only operate at fixed positions, and bipedal humanoid robots are too complex and costly to be widely deployed in actual manufacturing sites.
product.solution: FRIDAY is a mobile manipulator that moves on wheels and performs tasks with two arms and high-DoF hands. By forgoing bipedal locomotion, it achieves practical advantages in stability, battery life (4 hours of continuous operation, 24-hour operation with hot-swap battery), energy efficiency, and unit cost. It minimizes the simulation-to-reality gap with its own simulator (Holiday Sim) and world model (Holiday World).
key_features: 64 DoF (including 20 DoF per hand)
Ultra-lightweight robot hand (600g, 5kg payload per finger joint)
250Hz update rate, 0.05N sensitivity front tactile sensing
Wheeled differential drive base (max speed 1.9m/s)
24-hour uninterrupted operation with hot-swap battery system
Vision-Language-Skill (VLS) architecture
Proprietary GPU-accelerated physics simulator Holiday Sim and world model Holiday World
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Its proprietary VLS (Vision-Language-Skill) architecture does not directly convert large language model outputs into motor commands, but instead selects from pre-validated motor control primitives (grasping, screwing, moving, etc.). The tactile sensor uses a Hall-effect-based custom design, reducing the unit cost to about $20 (approximately 1/10 of the market price). It has open-sourced FlashSAC (a reinforcement learning algorithm).
product.target_customer: Automotive manufacturers, semiconductor producers, and logistics centers. Long-term planned expansion into service robot and home robot markets.
product.business_model: B2B model where FRIDAY hardware and control software are supplied, while field deployment and integration are handled by system integrator partners. Target unit price approx. KRW 100M ($67,000~$70,000, based on mass production).

direct_competitors.comparison: Develops bipedal humanoid Figure 02. Valued at $70B (est.), the most funded humanoid competitor. Lower DoF (approx. 24) compared to FRIDAY, price undisclosed.
Bipedal humanoid under development by Tesla. Approximately 28 DoF. Lower DoF than FRIDAY and not yet commercially available. Tesla's manufacturing and AI capabilities are strengths.
Logistics-specialized bipedal robot Digit. With approximately 16 DoF, limited manipulation capability compared to FRIDAY. Lease-based model at approx. $250,000 per year. Running a pilot with Amazon.
Chinese robot startup. G1 base price $16,000, the cheapest, but full-option costs are substantial. DoF 23-43. Inferior to FRIDAY in tactile sensing performance and hand dexterity.
Korean competitor. Wheeled two-armed robot RB-Y1 with cumulative sales over 130 units (as of end-2025). Similar design philosophy to FRIDAY but differentiated in DoF and tactile sensing.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: Design philosophy focused on wheeled base and high-DoF hands (62.5% of total DoF concentrated in hands) instead of bipedal walking. Own ultra-low-cost (approx. $20) high-sensitivity tactile sensor provides both cost competitiveness and manipulation performance edge over competitors. Deep understanding of manufacturing AI stemming from founder's experience at SuaLab and Cognex.
competitive_landscape.moat: Proprietary low-cost tactile sensor technology, full-stack software platform including VLS architecture (Holiday Sim, Holiday World, OASys), founder's proven deep tech startup and global M&A track record, and ability to invest in production facilities based on the largest Series A fund in Korea.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: FRIDAY is ahead of bipedal competitors in commercialization timeline (H2 2026) and target unit price (~$70,000), but has not yet disclosed confirmed customer orders or actual deployment data. Its production targets of 100 units in 2026 and 1,000 in 2027 are among the most aggressive mass-production roadmaps in the industry. The humanoid robot market itself is still early stage, and no company has proven sustainable unit economics.

physicl-2026.tagline: A synthetic data platform for rare situations where robots and vision models fail

founders.background: Previously founded and operated nfinite, a 3D commercialization platform, for six years. Experience building a system for creating 3D models of e-commerce products led to physical AI data.

physicl-2026.team_highlights: A team of 30, mostly 3D, simulation, and machine learning experts who have collaborated with the founder for over six years. Advisors include Thomas Wolf of Hugging Face and Christoph Lassner of World Labs.

product.summary: Provides 'Studio', a synthetic data platform that reproduces scenarios where robots or vision models are vulnerable using a 3D environment library based on real geometry and physical properties, and generates thousands of variant images and videos with accurate ground truth data.
product.problem_statement: Physical AI models (robot manipulation, world models, vision models) degrade sharply in rare 'long-tail' situations such as lighting, occlusion, and complex arrangements. Real captured data cannot sufficiently cover these rare cases, and human-labeled data often contains errors. Existing procedural randomization methods lack realism.
product.solution: Builds 3D scenes based on physical reality. When a user describes a failure scenario in natural language, the platform finds and suggests matching scenes from a library of 10,000 environments and 100,000 3D assets. Users control single conditions such as lighting, camera position, and object placement to generate variations, and output accurate depth, surface normal, segmentation, 2D bounding boxes, and camera poses 'by rendering' for every frame. The key is providing ground truth labels calculated from the scene itself, not by estimation or human labeling.
key_features: Input failure scenarios in natural language to suggest suitable 3D scenes
Library of 10,000 environments and 100,000 real-geometry-based 3D assets
Control single conditions such as lighting, camera, and object position (one condition at a time)
Directly generate depth, surface normal, instance/class segmentation, 2D boxes, and camera poses from rendering for every frame
Output images and videos up to 1920x1080 resolution
Object placement considering physical collisions and real-world scale
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Uses physically based rendering based on real 3D geometry and known materials. The technical differentiator is achieving both realism and control at the level of procedural randomization, along with accurate labels, unlike existing synthetic data. Emphasizes that 'labels are not estimated post-hoc but precisely determined at scene build time'.
product.target_customer: Robotics researchers learning robot manipulation policies, researchers developing computer vision models (perception, 3D vision), researchers training world models, and test engineers evaluating models before deployment; R&D organizations in physical AI.
product.business_model: Studio is currently in private beta and offered for free. A subscription or usage-based billing model is expected after official launch, but no official announcement has been made.

direct_competitors.comparison: The most comprehensive simulation platform, but requires high-performance GPU infrastructure and may have a high entry barrier compared to workflows for generating specific edge cases. Physicl provides an entry point specialized for edge case generation.

immaterial-2026.tagline: Material platform that creates high-density monoliths of MOF for industrial carbon capture

founders.background: Professor in the Department of Chemical Engineering at the University of Cambridge, leading the Adsorption and Advanced Materials Laboratory. Has over 15 years of research experience in the MOF field.
founders.notable_achievement: Spun out Immaterial from the University of Cambridge in 2015.

founders.background: Professional manager with experience in commercializing industrial decarbonization technologies.
founders.notable_achievement: Led the company through Series A2, attracting strategic investors such as JERA and UBE, and brought a multi-ton manufacturing facility online.

immaterial-2026.team_highlights: The core team includes CEO Mohammed Khan, CSO David Fairen-Jimenez, and process engineering experts such as Dr. Amir Farmahini. As of 2026, the estimated headcount is over 50 employees.

product.summary: Immaterial is a material platform that produces Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOF), a Nobel Prize-winning technology, in a monolith form for the first time in the world. It is applied to industrial point-source CO₂ capture, hydrogen storage, water harvesting, and HVAC energy savings.
product.problem_statement: Existing amine-based carbon capture technologies are energy-intensive and require large equipment, leading to high deployment costs in hard-to-abate sectors such as steel, cement, and chemicals. Powdered MOFs perform well but have low volumetric efficiency and are difficult to integrate into processes.
product.solution: Immaterial processes MOF crystals into monoliths (m-MOF) that are more than 10 times denser, maximizing carbon capture capacity per unit volume. This provides a solution directly applicable to pressure and temperature swing adsorption processes, dramatically reducing equipment size and capital expenditure.
key_features: High-density monolith MOF: Volume and weight performance improved by more than 2x compared to powder.
Wet-AI platform: Machine learning-based design combining digital material discovery and green synthesis optimization.
Multi-ton manufacturing capability: World's first m-MOF production line built in Cambridge, Sawston.
Process compatibility: Monolith structure that can be directly applied to existing swing adsorption systems.
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: The core innovation is the world's only MOF monolith processing technology. It compresses ordinary MOF powder into ultra-high-density crystals without binders, maintaining thermal and chemical stability while achieving over 100% performance improvement compared to conventional process pellets.
product.target_customer: Operators of large-scale CO₂-emitting industries (primary steel, refining, chemicals, cement), EPC companies, and energy firms.
product.business_model: Licenses or sells carbon capture units based on its self-produced m-MOF material to customers. It gains application references through pilot projects and then converts them into commercial contracts.

direct_competitors.comparison: Canada-based; commercialized carbon capture equipment using solid sorbents, but not MOF-based; primarily focused on filter-type capture systems.
Specialized in direct air capture (DAC); Immaterial focuses on point source capture, so the markets differ.
Develops both DAC and point source capture, but uses a potassium hydroxide wet process, which is a completely different technical approach.
UK-based; develops MOF-based carbon capture, but relies on powder form.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: Unique ability to produce MOF monoliths globally. This results in more than 2x volumetric efficiency compared to powdered MOFs and significantly improves process applicability.
competitive_landscape.moat: Patent-protected monolith processing technology and its proprietary 'Wet-AI' material design platform form the core entry barrier. Early multi-ton manufacturing capability and market access channels through strategic investors such as SLB, JERA, and UBE are also strong advantages.

product.solution: Through a proprietary technology platform comprising a farmer app, ERP, and customer e-commerce portal, it digitally coordinates the entire process: demand forecasting → farmer ordering → logistics → cold storage → sales → payment within three days. product.summary: Orchestra is a self-optimizing inference cloud that observes enterprise production inference traffic, automatically builds evaluations, and routes to cheaper specialized models, reducing costs by up to 100x.
product.problem_statement: Most AI companies always use the most expensive frontier models (Claude, GPT-4, etc.) even for repetitive tasks. product.solution: Orchestra proxies all enterprise inference with just a single URL change and uses traces to automatically build evaluations. When evaluations discover a specialized model (e.g., a Llama-based fine-tuned model) that outperforms frontier models on specific tasks, it automatically routes production traffic. The more it is used, the better the model becomes.
key_features: Unified inference gateway with a single URL change
Automatic evaluation (eval) generation based on real production traces
Automatic training and deployment of specialized models (based on open-weight models)
Over 97% cost reduction compared to frontier models (internal benchmark)
Customers own the model weights and can run them on their own cloud or on-premises
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Unlike existing routing solutions, Orchestra is not just a gateway but has a loop that converts actual task traces into evaluation data, continuously fine-tunes open-weight models based on that data, and automatically deploys them.
product.target_customer: AI-native startups and AI teams at large enterprises that spend hundreds of thousands of dollars or more per month on frontier model inference.
product.business_model: Usage-based pricing (per API call). It is estimated that they take a fee as a portion of what customers paid for frontier models, sharing in the savings.

Provides LLM gateway and observability tools, but lacks automatic model training and deployment.
